lessons.title: Making Watering Cans and Buckets
lessons.body: A good watering can is a farmer's daily tool. You can make one from a 5-litre plastic jerrycan or a metal bucket. For a plastic jerrycan, cut the top off with a hacksaw, leaving a handle. For the spout, use a 30 cm length of 12 mm PVC pipe. Drill a hole in the side of the can near the bottom, insert the pipe, and seal it with silicone or epoxy. The rose (sprinkler head) can be made from a tin can lid punched with a 2 mm nail in a grid pattern. Attach it to the spout with wire or tape. For a metal bucket, you can solder a spout made from a piece of galvanised pipe. Alternatively, make a simple bucket from a 20-litre oil tin. Clean it thoroughly with soap and water. Cut the top off with a chisel and hammer, leaving a rim. Attach a handle made from 6 mm rebar bent into a U-shape, or use heavy wire. For a watering can, punch holes in the bottom of a tin can and attach it to a wooden handle. In Africa, where materials are scarce, recycling is key. Use old plastic containers, metal tins, and rubber from tyres. A well-made watering can should hold 5-10 litres and pour a gentle stream. Test for leaks by filling with water. If it leaks, seal with beeswax or tar. These tools are essential for nursery beds, vegetable gardens, and young trees. With basic tools like a hacksaw, drill, and pliers, you can make one in under an hour. Remember to smooth sharp edges with a file to avoid cuts. A sturdy watering can saves water and reduces back strain compared to carrying a bucket.

lessons.title: Fabricating Drip Irrigation Components
lessons.body: Drip irrigation saves water by delivering it directly to plant roots. You can make a simple drip system using 16 mm black polyethylene (PE) pipe, available in most African farm supply shops. Start with a main line from your water source. Use a knife or pipe cutter to cut the pipe. For emitters, you can use micro-tubes: cut 30 cm lengths of 4 mm spaghetti tubing. Insert one end into a hole punched in the main line with a 4 mm punch. The other end goes to the plant. To regulate flow, tie a knot in the tube or insert a small plastic barb. Alternatively, make emitters from old bicycle inner tubes: cut small strips and puncture a pinhole. For a 100-metre row of tomatoes, you need about 200 emitters spaced 50 cm apart. You can also make a DIY drip line by punching holes directly in the 16 mm pipe every 30 cm. But holes can clog; use a filter made from a cloth bag or a 200-mesh screen. Connect the main line to a bucket or tank using a 13 mm barbed connector and a rubber washer. Gravity feed works if the tank is at least 1 metre above the field. For larger areas, use a small 12V pump. In dry areas like the Sahel, drip irrigation can increase yields by 50% with half the water. Maintain your system by flushing the lines weekly. Use vinegar to clear mineral deposits. With a punch, barb fittings, and end caps, you can assemble a drip kit for a 100 mÂ² garden in a day. Always use a filter to prevent clogging. This technology is affordable and scalable.

lessons.title: Building Sprinkler Systems
lessons.body: Sprinkler systems mimic rainfall and are good for leafy greens, carrots, and pasture. A simple homemade sprinkler can be made from a 2-litre plastic bottle. Puncture many small holes (1 mm) in the sides and bottom using a hot needle. Attach the bottle to a garden hose with a clamp. When water flows, it sprays in a circle. For a larger area, use a 20-litre bucket with holes drilled in the lid, placed on a raised platform. Connect a hose to the bucket and let gravity do the work. For a more efficient system, make a rotating sprinkler from a bicycle wheel. Weld or bolt a 1-metre length of 15 mm galvanised pipe to the hub. Drill holes along the pipe at 10 cm intervals, angled to create rotation. Connect the pipe to a hose via a swivel joint. Water pressure from a tank 3 metres high can run this. You can also use PVC pipes: build a frame with 20 mm PVC, drill 2 mm holes, and connect to a tap. For a 10 m x 10 m plot, you need about 20 sprinkler heads if using bottles, or one rotating sprinkler. Space sprinklers 3-4 metres apart. Test coverage by placing cups on the ground; aim for even distribution. In windy areas, use low-angle sprinklers. Maintenance: clean holes with a wire, and drain pipes before frost (not common in Africa, but in highlands). Sprinklers use more water than drip, so schedule irrigation early morning or evening to reduce evaporation. With basic plumbing skills, you can build a sprinkler system for under $20 using recycled materials.

lessons.title: Making Hand Pumps and Treadle Pumps
lessons.body: Hand pumps and treadle pumps lift water from shallow wells (up to 10 metres) and are vital where electricity is absent. A simple hand pump can be made from PVC pipe and a rubber plunger. Use a 50 mm PVC pipe as the cylinder. Cut a rubber disc from an old tyre inner tube to fit snugly inside the pipe; this is the plunger. Attach the plunger to a 10 mm steel rod. The rod goes up and down through a cap on the pipe. At the bottom, install a one-way valve (a flapper made from a rubber sheet and a hinge). When you pull up, water is drawn in; when you push down, the valve closes and water is pushed up. For the handle, use a metal lever attached to the rod. A treadle pump is more efficient for irrigation. It uses two cylinders and a treadle (foot pedal) mechanism. Build a frame from 40 mm angle iron. The cylinders are 100 mm PVC pipes. Connect the pistons to a crank shaft made from a bicycle axle. The treadle is a wooden plank pivoted in the middle. As you step, the crank turns, moving the pistons up and down. A well-made treadle pump can lift 1 litre per stroke and irrigate 0.2 hectares. Use leather or rubber cups for pistons. Seal all joints with Teflon tape or rubber gaskets. Test for leaks by pumping water and checking for air bubbles. These pumps are cheap to build (under $50) and easy to maintain. In many African countries, treadle pumps have doubled incomes for smallholder farmers. Always install a foot valve to keep water in the pipe. With basic welding and plumbing skills, you can make one in a day.

lessons.title: Constructing Water Tanks and Reservoirs
lessons.body: Water storage is critical for dry-season irrigation. You can build a ferrocement tank using cement, sand, wire mesh, and chicken wire. For a 2,000-litre tank, dig a circular hole 1.5 m deep and 1.5 m diameter. Build a frame with 6 mm rebar: vertical bars every 20 cm, and horizontal rings every 30 cm. Wrap chicken wire around the outside and inside, then apply a 1:3 cement-sand mortar in three layers. Cure for 7 days by keeping it wet. Alternatively, make a tank from a 200-litre drum cut in half and welded together, or use old plastic containers. For a reservoir, dig a pond and line it with clay or a 1 mm UV-resistant plastic liner. A 10 m x 10 m pond, 1 m deep, holds 100,000 litres. In areas with high evaporation, cover the pond with a shade net or floating balls. For a simple above-ground tank, use a 1,000-litre plastic tank (available in most towns) and place it on a raised platform of bricks or stones. Ensure the platform can support 1,000 kg. Connect an outlet pipe with a tap. For underground tanks, use concrete blocks or bricks, plastered with waterproof cement. Add a lid to prevent mosquitoes and evaporation. In Ethiopia, farmers build underground tanks to collect rainwater from roofs. A 20 mÂ² roof can collect 20,000 litres per year in a 1,000 mm rainfall area. Always include a first-flush diverter to keep dirty water out. With basic masonry skills, you can build a 5,000-litre tank for under $100. Regularly inspect for cracks and repair with mortar.

lessons.title: Maintenance of Irrigation Equipment
lessons.body: Regular maintenance extends the life of your irrigation tools and saves water. For watering cans and buckets, check for leaks and cracks. Seal small holes with silicone or beeswax. Replace broken handles with rebar or heavy wire. Clean the spout and rose weekly to remove algae and dirt. For drip systems, flush the main line and laterals every two weeks. Remove end caps and let water run for 5 minutes. Clean filters weekly: if using a screen filter, rinse it; if using a sand filter, backwash it. Use a 10% chlorine solution (1 litre bleach to 10 litres water) to clear organic clogging, then flush with clean water. For sprinklers, clean holes with a fine wire. Check for worn nozzles and replace them. Lubricate rotating parts with grease. For hand and treadle pumps, inspect the plunger and valves every month. Replace worn rubber cups. Tighten all bolts and check the handle for cracks. Lubricate the pivot points with oil. For tanks and reservoirs, inspect for cracks and leaks. Patch with cement mortar or epoxy. Clean the tank annually: drain, scrub with a brush and bleach solution, then rinse. Remove sediment from the bottom. For ponds, remove weeds and debris. Check the liner for tears. In all cases, keep a maintenance log. Train all users on proper operation. A well-maintained drip system can last 10 years; a neglected one fails in one season. Use the right tools: a pipe cutter, spanners, and a wire brush. Store equipment under cover when not in use. In Africa, where spare parts may be scarce, learn to make your own gaskets from old inner tubes. Preventive maintenance is cheaper than repairs. Spend 30 minutes each week checking your system; it will pay off with better yields and less water waste.

quiz.q: What is the best material for making a watering can rose?
options: A) A tin can lid with punched holes
D) A metal plate with drilled holes
quiz.explanation: A tin can lid punched with a 2 mm nail is a simple and effective rose for a watering can.

quiz.q: How can you seal a leak in a plastic watering can?
quiz.explanation: Silicone or epoxy provides a durable waterproof seal for plastic containers.

quiz.q: What size PVC pipe is commonly used for a drip irrigation main line?
quiz.explanation: 16 mm black polyethylene pipe is standard for drip irrigation laterals and main lines.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a filter in a drip irrigation system?
options: B) To prevent clogging of emitters
quiz.explanation: A filter removes particles that can clog the small emitters.

quiz.q: How high should a water tank be for gravity-fed drip irrigation?
options: A) At least 1 metre above the field
quiz.explanation: A height of 1 metre provides enough pressure for gravity-fed drip systems.

quiz.q: What is a common material for making homemade sprinkler holes?
quiz.explanation: A hot needle melts clean holes in plastic bottles for sprinklers.

quiz.q: What is the recommended spacing for sprinklers in a 10x10 m plot?
quiz.explanation: Sprinklers spaced 3-4 metres apart give even coverage.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of drip irrigation over sprinklers?
quiz.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to roots, reducing evaporation and waste.

quiz.q: What material can be used to make a plunger for a hand pump?
options: A) Rubber from an inner tube
quiz.explanation: Rubber from an old tyre inner tube is flexible and seals well for a plunger.

quiz.q: What is the typical lift capacity of a treadle pump?
quiz.explanation: Treadle pumps can lift water from depths up to about 10 metres.

quiz.q: What is a common material for making a ferrocement tank?
options: A) Cement, sand, and wire mesh
quiz.explanation: Ferrocement tanks are built with cement mortar over wire mesh and rebar.

quiz.q: How long should a ferrocement tank be cured?
quiz.explanation: Curing for 7 days keeps the cement moist for proper strength.

quiz.q: What is a first-flush diverter used for in rainwater harvesting?
options: B) To discard the first dirty water
quiz.explanation: A first-flush diverter sends the initial dirty roof runoff away from the tank.

quiz.q: How often should you flush a drip irrigation system?
quiz.explanation: Flushing every two weeks prevents sediment and clogging.

quiz.q: What is a simple method to clean organic clogging in drip lines?
quiz.explanation: A 10% chlorine solution (1 litre bleach to 10 litres water) clears organic matter.

quiz.q: What should you use to lubricate hand pump pivot points?
quiz.explanation: Oil is suitable for lubricating moving parts of hand pumps.

quiz.q: What is the recommended spacing for emitters in a drip line for tomatoes?
quiz.explanation: Emitters spaced 50 cm apart are typical for row crops like tomatoes.

quiz.q: What is a common problem with homemade drip emitters?
quiz.explanation: Small holes in homemade emitters easily clog with debris.

quiz.q: What material is commonly used for a treadle pump frame?
quiz.explanation: Angle iron provides a strong, durable frame for treadle pumps.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a foot valve in a hand pump?
options: A) To keep water in the pipe
quiz.explanation: A foot valve holds water in the pipe so the pump doesn't lose prime.

quiz.q: How can you prevent evaporation from a small reservoir?
options: A) Cover with a shade net
quiz.explanation: A shade net reduces evaporation by blocking sun and wind.

quiz.q: What is a cheap liner material for a farm pond?
quiz.explanation: Clay is a traditional and low-cost liner for ponds where available.

quiz.q: What is the first step in maintaining a sprinkler system?
options: A) Clean holes with a wire
quiz.explanation: Cleaning holes with a wire removes blockages and restores spray pattern.

quiz.q: What should you do if a tank develops a crack?
options: A) Patch with cement mortar or epoxy
quiz.explanation: Cement mortar or epoxy is a durable repair for cracks in tanks.

quiz.q: Why is preventive maintenance important for irrigation equipment?
options: A) It is cheaper than repairs
quiz.explanation: Preventive maintenance avoids costly breakdowns and extends equipment life.

quiz.q: What is a common source of rubber for making pump cups?
quiz.explanation: Old tyre inner tubes provide durable rubber for pump cups.

quiz.q: How much water can a 20 mÂ² roof collect in a 1,000 mm rainfall area?
quiz.explanation: 20 mÂ² x 1 m = 20 mÂ³ = 20,000 litres per year.

quiz.q: What is the recommended frequency for inspecting hand pump valves?
quiz.explanation: Monthly inspection catches wear before it causes failure.

quiz.q: What is a simple way to test sprinkler coverage?
options: A) Place cups on the ground
quiz.explanation: Cups collect water to show if distribution is even.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of a treadle pump over a hand pump?
options: B) It can lift more water with less effort
quiz.explanation: Treadle pumps use leg muscles, which are stronger, to lift more water.
